profile.name: The Coca-Cola Company
profile.summary: The Coca-Cola Company, a beverage company, manufactures and sells various nonalcoholic beverages in the United States and internationally. The company provides Trademark Coca-Cola, sparkling soft drinks and flavors; water, sports, coffee, and tea; juice, value-added dairy, and plant-based beverages; and emerging beverages. It also offers beverage concentrates and syrups, as well as fountain syrups to fountain retailers comprising restaurants and convenience stores. The company sells its products under the Coca-Cola, Diet Coke/Coca-Cola Light, Coca-Cola Zero Sugar, caffeine free Diet Coke, Cherry Coke, Fanta, Sprite, Simply, Fanta Orange, Fanta Zero Orange, Fanta Zero Sugar, Fanta Apple, Sprite Zero Sugar, Simply Orange, Simply Apple, Simply Grapefruit, Fresca, Schweppes, Thums Up, Aquarius, Ayataka, BODYARMOR, Ciel, Costa, Crystal, Dasani, Fuze Tea, Georgia, glacéau smartwater, glacéau vitaminwater, Gold Peak, I LOHAS, Powerade, Topo Chico, Core Power, Del Valle, fairlife, innocent, Maaza, Minute Maid, Minute Maid Pulpy, Santa Clara, and dogadan brands. It operates through a network of independent bottling partners, distributors, wholesalers, and retailers, as well as through bottling and distribution operators. The Coca-Cola Company was founded in 1886 and is headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia.

trends.claim: Health-driven demand for zero-sugar and diet carbonated soft drinks is rising as of July 2026, pressuring sugary CSDs while lifting better-for-you variants.
trends.why: Shifts mix within Sparkling Soft Drinks; KO's zero-sugar portfolio can offset core sugar volume decline.
trends.quote: Demand for zero-sugar and diet carbonated soft drink formulations is increasing owing to rising consumer awareness of obesity and metabolic health risks
trends.speed_basis: Published July 2026; demand shift already noted.
trends.impact_basis: Core Sparkling Soft Drinks stream; mix shift decides revenue/margin.
trends.theme_definition: Consumers shift to lower-sugar, functional drinks, forcing beverage makers to reformulate portfolios.

trends.claim: US functional and health-oriented drink demand is accelerating category diversification as of June 2026, expanding addressable demand.
trends.why: Functional demand lifts KO's water, sports, coffee/tea and energy lines, supporting price/mix.
trends.quote: Rising consumer preference for functional and health-oriented drinks across demographics is accelerating category diversification.
trends.size_basis: US non-alcoholic beverages $195.46B in 2026; functional share not stated.
trends.theme_definition: Consumers increasingly buy drinks with functional health benefits, expanding beverage categories beyond refreshment.

trends.claim: Non-carbonated soft drinks are forecast to grow at a 6.4% CAGR from 2026 to 2033.
trends.why: Lifts KO's non-carbonated portfolio, offsetting slower carbonated volume growth.
trends.quote: growing at a CAGR of 6.4% from 2026 to 2033
trends.speed_basis: Forecast period starts 2026; growth already underway.
trends.theme_definition: Consumers move from carbonated sugary drinks to still, hydrating, and functional non-carbonated beverages.

trends.claim: US soda per capita consumption has declined roughly 10–15%, as of August 2026, constraining volume.
trends.why: Limits US volume growth in KO's largest CSD market, forcing reliance on price/mix.
trends.quote: per capita consumption has declined by roughly 10–15%
trends.size_basis: no exact size in evidence; world's largest CSD market.
trends.speed_basis: Decline over past decade; current as of August 2026.
trends.impact_basis: Directly hits Sparkling Soft Drinks, KO's largest stream.
trends.theme_definition: Per-person consumption of sugary carbonated drinks falls in mature markets, pressuring volume.

trends.claim: In June 2026, major QSRs are expanding refreshers, flavored sodas and craft-style dispensed beverages, lifting foodservice beverage demand.
trends.why: More QSR beverage launches increase concentrate and syrup sales through KO's foodservice system.
trends.quote: Sonic, McDonald’s, Chick-fil-A, and Whataburger are all expanding their assortment of refreshers, flavored sodas, lemonades, floats and craft-style beverage formats
trends.impact_basis: Reaches Sparkling Soft Drinks via foodservice dispensed channel.
trends.theme_definition: Restaurant chains broaden dispensed drink menus, increasing fountain beverage demand.

trends.claim: As of August 2026, Coca-Cola is scaling white-label foodservice drinks, with lemonade already in more than 40,000 dispensers.
trends.why: Expands foodservice revenue via equipment and white-label supply, deepening customer lock-in.
trends.quote: A white-label lemonade already runs through more than 40,000 dispensers, some of it sold as Wendy’s Dave’s Craft Lemonade.
trends.speed_basis: Unbranded energy arrives with operators in first half of 2027.
trends.impact_basis: Adds foodservice revenue but small versus total KO.
trends.theme_definition: Beverage makers supply unbranded drinks and equipment to restaurants seeking exclusive menus.

trends.claim: As of August 2026, more c-store chains are considering vertical integration to cut costs and control supply, shifting channel power.
trends.why: Retailer integration can bypass suppliers, pressure margins and shelf space for KO brands.
trends.quote: more chains of all sizes are considering how various levels of vertical integration can help improve efficiency, strengthen supply chains and create a competitive advantage.
trends.speed_basis: Chains considering; adoption not yet quantified.
trends.impact_basis: Affects c-store channel across all beverage streams.
trends.theme_definition: Retailers bring distribution and production in-house to cut costs and control supply.

trends.claim: As of September 2026, health pressure and private-label competition keep rising, challenging Coca-Cola's pricing power.
trends.why: Private label and health shifts can slow volume and limit price increases across KO's portfolio.
trends.quote: health pressure and private-label competition keep rising
trends.impact_basis: Threatens pricing/mix across all beverage streams.
trends.theme_definition: Retailer-owned brands gain share, pressuring branded beverage pricing and volume.

trends.claim: As of April 2026, Coca-Cola's CFO warned higher aluminum and PET prices would hit bottlers if sustained.
trends.why: Higher packaging input costs squeeze bottler margins and may pass through to KO's system economics.
trends.quote: bottlers would have greater impact if higher aluminum and pet prices sustain
trends.size_basis: no dollar magnitude; packaging is critical input
trends.speed_basis: CFO comments April 2026; disruption already occurred.
trends.impact_basis: Affects all packaged beverage streams via bottler cost base.
trends.theme_definition: Rising aluminum and PET costs raise packaging expenses across the beverage supply chain.

trends.claim: In September 2026, the Coca-Cola system announced $10 billion of US infrastructure investment for 2026–2030 to expand production and distribution.
trends.why: Expands US capacity and distribution, supporting volume growth but adding system capital intensity.
trends.quote: The Coca-Cola system plans to invest USD$10 billion in US infrastructure between 2026 and 2030
trends.speed_basis: Investment period starts 2026; projects already announced.
trends.impact_basis: Supports US volume across all streams; mostly bottler-funded.
trends.theme_definition: Beverage makers and bottlers invest in production and distribution capacity to meet demand.

trends.claim: In the quarter reported by May 2026, Coca-Cola's gross margin fell about 30 basis points on tea and coffee commodity pressures.
trends.why: Higher tea and coffee input costs compress gross margin in that stream.
trends.quote: comparable gross margin still declined by around 30 basis points, mainly due to commodity pressures in tea and coffee
trends.size_basis: about 30 basis points of gross margin decline
trends.impact_basis: Hits Water, Sports, Coffee & Tea gross margin.
trends.theme_definition: Rising coffee and tea input costs squeeze margins for beverage makers.

trends.claim: As of February 2026, Coca-Cola's asset-light franchise model targets about 60 basis points annual margin expansion and 93% cash conversion.
trends.why: Franchise-led structure lowers owned-asset risk and supports margin and cash flow.
trends.quote: about 60 basis points of annual margin expansion and 93 percent cash conversion
trends.size_basis: about 60 basis points annual margin expansion
trends.impact_basis: Affects total company margin and cash conversion.
trends.theme_definition: Beverage companies shift to franchise bottling to lower capital intensity and lift margins.
